[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 14, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 14 at 5680 Badura Ave, Las Vegas, NV. Sourced from DataCenterMap, a single aggregator directory, not independently corroborated by a second source this session.  Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 14 sits within the Las Vegas Core Campus, a cluster of eleven operating data centers spanning over two million square feet in Clark County. The operator publishes no power capacity, rack count, or IT load for this specific facility or for the campus as a whole. Without published specifications, the site's scale and current readiness for AI workloads cannot be determined from operator disclosures.

Nevada has twenty-six mapped data center facilities, but only two publish power consumption figures to public spec pages, totaling 10.37 megawatts across the state. This facility ranks third in the state by published megawatts, though it publishes none itself, placing it below two other sites with disclosed capacity. The state context does not permit ranking by actual capacity, only by sites that have made figures public.

The Las Vegas Core Campus was founded on fiber backbone infrastructure and has operated continuously since 2002. The operator, now privately held by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors as of December 2022, does not publish power, cooling, or equipment specifications on its official locations page. Whether this facility matters to AI scaling cannot be assessed from published data.
